introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (headed "One hour 30 minutes" on page 2): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (40 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (50 minutes): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State what is meant by a signal.

The signals television stations transmit as space wave are mostly VHF and UHF signals.

(ii) Write out the full meanings of VHF and UHF.

(iii) State and explain whether it is VHF or UHF signals that transmit more energy. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **signal** is a physical quantity (a varying voltage, current, light pulse or electromagnetic wave) that varies in a way that carries information (sound, picture, data) from a source to a receiver.

(ii) **VHF** = Very High Frequency (about $30$ to $300\ \mathrm{MHz}$). **UHF** = Ultra High Frequency (about $300\ \mathrm{MHz}$ to $3\ \mathrm{GHz}$).

(iii) **UHF signals transmit more energy.** Both are electromagnetic waves, which carry energy in photons of energy $E = hf$. UHF has the higher frequency, so each photon carries more energy and, for a given number of photons per second, the wave carries more power.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A radio receiver has many component parts, some of which are the LC loop and the Demodulator (both underlined in the paper). State the uses of the underlined components of a simple radio receiver.

(ii) In terms of *noise interference, broadcast range and bandwidth*, state how AM signals differ from FM signals. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **LC loop (tuned circuit):** an inductor and a capacitor in parallel, used to **select** the wanted station. The aerial picks up the signals of many stations at once; the loop responds strongly only at its resonant frequency $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$, which is set equal to the carrier frequency of the wanted station by varying the capacitance $C$, so other stations are rejected.

**Demodulator (detector):** it **recovers the audio (information) signal** from the modulated carrier wave: a diode rectifies the signal and a capacitor smooths it, removing the high-frequency carrier and leaving the audio-frequency signal which is amplified and sent to the loudspeaker.

(ii)

| | AM (amplitude modulation) | FM (frequency modulation) |
|---|---|---|
| Noise and interference | More affected: noise and interference (lightning, electrical machinery) change the amplitude of the wave and so are heard as noise | Much less affected: the information is in the frequency, so amplitude variations are removed (limited) at the receiver |
| Broadcast range | Greater: used at lower frequencies (long, medium and short waves) that follow the ground or are reflected by the ionosphere, so reach hundreds or thousands of kilometres | Smaller: VHF travels in a straight line (line of sight), so the range is limited to about $50$ to $100\ \mathrm{km}$ |
| Bandwidth | Narrow (about $10\ \mathrm{kHz}$ per station), so many stations fit in the band | Wide (about $200\ \mathrm{kHz}$ per station), which allows high-quality sound but fewer stations in the band |

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) In front of a certain tall concrete building backing a cell site, cell phone reception is very poor. List two reasons for this observed fact.

(ii) What does it mean to say that a cell phone is roaming? *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Two reasons:

1. The concrete building (especially with steel reinforcement) **absorbs and reflects** the microwave signal from the cell site, so little of it passes through to the front of the building.
2. The building **blocks the direct line of sight** to the cell site, and the wavelength used by mobile phones (a few tens of centimetres) is small compared with the building, so there is little diffraction round it: the front of the building lies in a radio shadow. (Waves reflected from other buildings may arrive out of phase and interfere destructively, which also weakens the signal.)

(ii) A cell phone is **roaming** when it is used outside the coverage area of its home network operator and connects through the cell sites of another (visited) network, for example in another region or country. The visited network identifies the phone with the home network, so calls, messages and data continue to work (usually at a different charge), and the phone is handed from cell to cell as it moves.
